'''Doxford International''' is a {{convert|125|acre|adj=on}} business park located at the A19 / A690 interchange on the outskirts of [[Sunderland, Tyne and Wear|Sunderland]], in the [[North East England|North East of England]]. Previously it was a [[Greenfield land|greenfield site]], it was designated as an [[Urban Enterprise Zone|Enterprise Zone]] in 1990 in response to the decline of the area's former [[Shipbuilding|ship building]] and [[coal mining]] industries. A partnership between [[City of Sunderland|Sunderland City Council]] and Goodman Property (formerly Akeler Developments Ltd.) has seen the creation of {{convert|1350000|sqft|m2|abbr=on}} of high-specification offices, with the private sector partner investing around £200 million. The first buildings were completed in 1992,<ref name=Bowmer/> providing accommodation for a range of businesses that have played a key role in the regeneration of the City.

At the entrance to the development stands the sculpture ''Quintisection'' by the sculptor [[Robert Erskine (sculptor)|Robert Erskine]] FRSS. Standing {{convert|26|ft|m|abbr=on|adj=mid|in height}} and {{convert|14.5|ft|m|abbr=on|adj=mid|wide}}, it is made in wrought stainless steel, and is based upon a huge cross-section of an ocean liner. Commissioned by Doxford International Business Park, ''Quintesection'' is a sculpture to mark the shipbuilding industry of the North East.

The availability of telecommunications and a skilled workforce has been instrumental in the success of Doxford International, which is now a location for corporate HQs and contact centres serving the financial and customer service sectors. Around 8,000 people are now employed by a range of blue chip companies.{{Citation needed|date=July 2009}}

One business that located on Doxford International is mobile phone operator [[EE Limited]], which has a customer support centre that now employs around 1,000 people. The site operates as a switching centre, underpinning the company's network between Leeds and Edinburgh.

Also on Doxford International, EDS has established a secure data centre. Citifinancial {{En dash}} part of the US-based [[CitiGroup]] {{En dash}} was one of the businesses that has reinvested in Doxford International, with an expansion project that brought additional jobs to Sunderland. [[CitiGroup]] no longer have a presence at Doxford, leaving the site in 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=E-mail has call centre staff fearing for jobs |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/north-east-news/e-mail-call-centre-staff-fearing-1482743 |access-date=1 February 2026 |work=Chronicle Live |date=27 February 2013 |language=en}}</ref>

[[EDF Energy]] has based its main contact centre at Doxford,<ref>{{cite news |title=EDF Energy announces centre of excellence |url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/7008922.edf-energy-announces-centre-excellence/ |access-date=1 February 2026 |work=The Northern Echo |date=20 November 2003 |language=en}}</ref> originally trading at the site as London Electricity.

As well as small retail outlets such as [[Greggs the bakers]] and a [[Subway (restaurant)|Subway]] outlet, the Sunderland Health & Racquet Club operated by [[David Lloyd Leisure]] provides leisure facilities.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gym with swimming pool in Sunderland {{!}} Health Club {{!}} David Lloyd Clubs |url=https://www.davidlloyd.co.uk/clubs/sunderland/ |website=www.davidlloyd.co.uk |access-date=1 February 2026 |language=en-gb}}</ref> 

In 2002, the park won the Commercial Award, "for outstanding contribution from business and retail interests", at the 2002 [[Britain in Bloom]] Awards presentation ceremony in [[Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Industrial estate takes bloom prize |url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/7059155.industrial-estate-takes-bloom-prize/ |access-date=1 February 2026 |work=The Northern Echo |date=20 September 2002 |language=en}}</ref>

A 500-space car park was planned within the park in 2020.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harrison |first1=James |title=Chiefs defend 500-space car park plans after critic brands project 'environmental vandalism' |url=https://www.sunderlandecho.com/news/politics/council/sunderland-chiefs-defend-500-space-car-park-plans-near-doxford-international-after-critic-brands-project-environmental-vandalism-2931970 |access-date=1 February 2026 |work=Sunderland Echo |date=4 August 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2025, UK Management College submitted proposals for a site in Doxford International Business Park, to convert an empty office block so that it could offer courses in health and social care and fashion design.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sunderland college campus plan submitted for business park |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c7vl57vzg2vo |website=BBC News |access-date=1 February 2026 |date=27 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Binding |first1=Chris |title=Sunderland Doxford Park college campus plans resbumitted |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cdd565p5vqlo |access-date=1 February 2026 |work=BBC News |date=27 November 2025}}</ref>
